claims.statement: The Bifrost llm-gateway (maximhq/bifrost:v2.2.6, APP_PORT 8080) is the only egress path for LLM calls: agents run on the egress-less internal network, reach LLMs only via llm-replay (SANDMAN_LLM_BASE_URL http://llm-replay:8000/openai) which forwards to http://llm-gateway:8080/openai, and only the gateway sits on the egress network; provider keys live only in deploy/secrets/gateway.env read solely by the gateway container.

Gateway governance is declared in deploy/gateway/config.json mounted read-only at /app/data/config.json: enforce_auth_on_inference true, enable_logging true, SQLite config/log stores in the gateway-data volume, providers openai/openrouter/ollama with env.* key values, admin auth (admin / env.BIFROST_ADMIN_PASSWORD), ten virtual keys, six budgets and two rate limits; the file contains no secret values and the gateway starts healthy with empty provider keys.

Each LLM-using component gets a second Ollama-only virtual key <component>-local whose provider_configs list only the ollama provider, so local-only projects cannot reach cloud providers; the gateway rejects a -local key on a cloud route with HTTP 403 provider_blocked (spike T0.4 check 12), enforcing the policy for code the project does not control.

The ten virtual keys are: cloud keys vk-orchestrator, vk-extraction, vk-tlr, vk-inconsistency, vk-query and vk-experiments (openai/openrouter/ollama), plus Ollama-only vk-extraction-local, vk-tlr-local, vk-inconsistency-local and vk-query-local; values are env.VK_* references in gateway.env, and gen-secrets.sh writes the same values into per-component compose secrets llm_key_<component>[_local] mounted into exactly one service each (vk-experiments has no compose secret — it is for evaluation scripts). LLM-using plugins get plugin-<id> and plugin-<id>-local keys added by the operator (none in the committed config).

Budgets are monthly (reset_duration 1M) USD limits per virtual key: b-orchestrator 10, b-extraction 20, b-tlr 50, b-inconsistency 30, b-query 10, b-experiments 50 (placeholders to be set by the operator); rate limits are rl-default (60 requests/min, 200,000 tokens/hour) and rl-heavy (300 requests/min, 2,000,000 tokens/hour), with rl-heavy attached to the tlr, inconsistency and experiments keys (and their -local variants); the -local Ollama keys carry rate limits but no budget.

Budgets and rate limits must be edited in deploy/gateway/config.json (then restart llm-gateway, since the file is mounted read-only): in Bifrost v2.2.6 the admin UI cannot save a standalone virtual-key budget (the form sends an empty reset duration and fails with 'invalid reset duration format:'), although the 1M value in config.json itself is valid.

Gateway error semantics measured in spike T0.4: missing or unknown virtual key → HTTP 401 (enforce_auth_on_inference); exhausted budget → HTTP 402 body budget_exceeded, with the first crossing call still served because Bifrost counts spending afterwards; rate limit → HTTP 429 body request_limited with no Retry-After header; -local key on a cloud route → HTTP 403 provider_blocked; management API, request log and /metrics without admin credentials → HTTP 401 (also from a container on the internal network). Python OpenAiLlmClient maps 402 to BudgetExceededError, which the skill layer reports as non-retryable SkillError BUDGET_EXCEEDED so the orchestrator blocks the workflow; 429 stays with the SDK's own retries.

Python ModelSelector (sandman_agent.llm) reads the routes from models.yaml and implements the project LLM policy: chat_model/embed_model return chat-local/embed-local for policy local-only else chat-default/embed-default, and client(policy) returns an OpenAiLlmClient with the cloud key or, for local-only, the local key with local_only=True — raising PolicyError when a local-only project has no local key configured; with local_only=True the client refuses any route not ending in -local (PolicyError), and OpenAiLlmClient maps a response_schema to OpenAI response_format json_schema (strict true), sets user=run_id, forwards telemetry trace_headers(), defaults temperature to 0.0, and returns the gateway-resolved model name in ChatResponse.resolved_model. The Java mirror is LlmAccess.forPolicy (no Java LlmClient by design, ADR-0010 D-7), which configures LangChain4j in approach/detector adapters with the same -local restriction and a toString() that never prints the key.

Agents never hard-code provider models: logical routes in config/llm/models.yaml (mounted read-only at /config/llm/models.yaml, value SANDMAN_LLM_MODELS_FILE) map chat-default, chat-alt, chat-local, embed-default and embed-local to gateway model names of the form openai/<model>, openrouter/<vendor>/<model> or ollama/<model>:<tag>; concrete models are not committed yet (open TODO), no cross-provider fallbacks are configured, and the gateway-resolved model name is recorded on each Run (Run.model keeps the route, Run.resolvedModel the resolved name).

Ollama runs only under the compose local-llm profile (ollama/ollama:0.35.1) on the llm-local network — internal:true with only the gateway and Ollama as members, so local models are reachable only through the gateway — plus the egress network for model pulls; the gateway reaches it at http://ollama:11434 via the provider entry's ollama_key_config.url with an empty key value.

The gateway admin UI and request log are published on 127.0.0.1:8081 (compose mapping 127.0.0.1:8081:8080) behind the governance.auth_config login (username admin, password env.BIFROST_ADMIN_PASSWORD, generated by gen-secrets.sh into secrets/gateway_admin_password and never mounted into agents); the request log uses the SQLite logs_store, /metrics exposes about 20 bifrost_* series (cost_total, input/output_tokens_total, error_requests_total, latency histograms), and the request log does not store the traceparent header — LLM calls must be correlated via OpenTelemetry and the user field (run id), with 30-day retention as a still-unverified design target.

deploy/gen-secrets.sh (idempotent, never overwrites) generates the VK_* virtual-key values into deploy/secrets/gateway.env together with BIFROST_ENCRYPTION_KEY and the BIFROST_ADMIN_PASSWORD (which satisfies Bifrost's >=12-character upper/lower/digit/special policy), writes the same VK values into per-component secret files llm_key_<component>[_local], and leaves OPENAI_API_KEY/OPENROUTER_API_KEY empty for the operator to fill in gateway.env; only the llm-gateway container reads gateway.env (env_file), so provider and admin credentials never enter agent containers.

The llm-replay proxy (services/llm-replay, Starlette, port 8000, upstream http://llm-gateway:8080/openai) sits between all callers and the gateway: modes live/record/replay from SANDMAN_LLM_MODE, cassette key sha256 of the RFC 8785-canonical request body excluding user/stream/stream_options, only chat/completions and embeddings recordable (streaming rejected with 400 streaming_not_supported), replay misses return 404 replay_miss, and it forwards the caller's Authorization header unchanged — it holds no keys itself; because the cassette key contains the gateway model name, re-pointing a route invalidates recordings.

Project.llmPolicy (enum cloud-allowed / local-only, required in contracts/kg/schema.yaml, set at project creation via the extraction-agent API and stored on the Project node) is enforced twice: clients pick the -local key and *-local routes for local-only projects (Python ModelSelector / Java LlmAccess / plugins via the llmPolicy field of PluginExtractInput and PluginDetectInput, where a plugin that cannot comply must error rather than call a cloud model), and the gateway independently rejects the Ollama-only key on cloud providers (403 provider_blocked).

ADR-0004 chose Bifrost (single container, SQLite default, Apache-2.0, OpenAI-compatible, virtual keys with budgets and rate limits in the OSS build) with the LiteLLM proxy as recorded fallback (change triggers: runtime-gated governance or missing provider); the decision was proposed until spike T0.4 verified virtual keys, budgets (HTTP 402 budget_exceeded), rate limits (HTTP 429 request_limited), admin auth, -local key isolation and keyless startup in OSS v2.2.6, and was accepted on 2026-10-07.
